threats.control: Eligibility starts from the retained active membership-acceptance binding, derives later restriction events append-only, and requires the current Circle Core snapshot to equal the derived lifecycle head.
threats.residual: The current Core membership object remains a snapshot surface; correctness depends on retaining the complete eligibility event chain and historical acceptance binding.

threats.control: The v0 eligibility lifecycle permits only strict role-set narrowing; a lifecycle event cannot add, restore, or substitute a role even when that role exists in the charter.
threats.residual: Future role grants or restoration require a separately authorized governance procedure and are intentionally unsupported here.

threats.control: Membership suspension is one-way in v0; resume is unsupported so a lifecycle record cannot silently restore eligibility after suspension.
threats.residual: A practical future resume procedure needs explicit actor, collective-authorization, notice, appeal, and credential-currentness semantics.

threats.control: Revocation and voluntary exit are terminal, reject all later eligibility events, and must bind exactly one matching Circle Core exit record at the same effective time.
threats.residual: The contract does not establish whether the revocation or exit process was legitimate, voluntary, procedurally fair, or legally effective.

threats.control: Role narrowing is resolved by event time and checked against the charter active at that time, so later narrowing does not rewrite an earlier eligibility state.
threats.residual: This slice does not yet retrofit every Circle record-authorization call site to require the new resolver; that atomic integration remains a promotion blocker.

threats.control: Credential eligibility composes the preserved hardened credential lifecycle with membership state at the exact use time and requires the selected credential to be active and authentication-eligible.
threats.residual: The carried-forward credential lifecycle still does not prove who authorized initial credential issuance, suspension/resume, replacement-device admission, or recovery.

threats.control: The eligibility assessment explicitly sets credential_possession_verified false and treats authenticatedPrincipal as external assurance rather than self-authenticating input.
threats.residual: A future Hypervisor service path must cryptographically authenticate possession of the selected member credential and bind that result to the principal and request.

threats.control: Historical acceptance, membership lifecycle, credential lifecycle, selected credential, and authenticated-principal input must all bind the same Circle, membership, and principal identifiers.
threats.residual: Identifier agreement does not prove human identity, legal identity, unique-personhood, or freedom from account compromise.

threats.control: The preserved credential lifecycle rejects post-compromise issuance and derives credentials on a compromised device as ineligible for later authentication use.
threats.residual: The contract cannot detect an unreported compromise and does not attest secure hardware custody.

threats.control: Every eligibility assessment binds an exact as_of time plus membership-lifecycle, credential-lifecycle, historical-ledger, policy, and governing-charter digests.
threats.residual: The assessment is inert; a future admission path must reject stale assessments by recomputing current state or enforcing a bounded authenticated freshness rule.

threats.control: The eligibility result carries no runtime or external-effect authority and cannot append to Grid, mint a Circle decision, or invoke Gateway, Hypervisor, or Sandbox effects.
threats.residual: Runtime promotion must bind member eligibility and record authorization into the same Hypervisor-issued Grid admission capability so a caller cannot mix evidence from different states.

threats.control: The contract makes no human-identity, legal-identity, governance-legitimacy, or coercion-free-participation claim.
threats.residual: Distinct principals or valid credentials can still represent Sybils, shared control, coercion, malware, deception, or captured governance.

promotion_blockers: Define authorized Circle role-grant and membership-resume procedures before any lifecycle operation may widen eligibility.
Define credential issuance, credential resume, replacement-device admission, and recovery authorization rather than treating structurally valid credential records as self-authorizing.
Implement Hypervisor-bound proof of possession for the selected Circle member credential and bind it to authenticated principal, Circle, membership, request digest, and freshness window.
Retrofit Circle record authorization to resolve membership status and roles from this append-only lifecycle at each record event time rather than relying on the current snapshot compatibility path.
Bind the exact member-eligibility assessment and record-authorization assessment into one Hypervisor-issued Circle Grid admission capability and deterministic Grid event.
Make the eligibility-plus-authorization-plus-admission composition the only service-level Circle append path; direct persistence helpers must remain inaccessible to runtime callers.
Persist eligibility restriction events through the replay-safe Circle Grid path with deterministic identity and atomic head ordering before treating the lifecycle as durable runtime state.
Define electorate handling for suspension, revocation, exit, and role narrowing during an already-open proposal without retroactively rewriting valid earlier participation.
Add accessible member-facing explanations for active, suspended, narrowed, revoked, exited, credential-compromised, and credential-ineligible states.
Complete independent security, privacy, coercion, Sybil, recovery, capture, and governance review before real Circle authentication or decision use.
